title: Codex developer cockpit
context: Codex is the only AI coding environment in the core curriculum. Configure it with safe instructions, project context, GitHub access, current documentation habits, browser evidence, and Vercel diagnostics before building client work.

stories.title: Install and orient Codex in the curriculum repository
stories.outcome: Codex can inspect the correct local repository under understood permission boundaries.
stories.context: Install and sign in using official Codex documentation. Start from the curriculum clone and use status, permissions, and review features before asking for changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Node 24, npm, Git, GitHub CLI, and Codex versions are recorded with sensitive output removed
Codex starts in the curriculum Git root and accurately explains the repository map
The learner explains permissions and chooses a safe setting for exploratory versus mutating tasks

expectations.security: Never publish login/token output; review permissions before work.
expectations.privacy: No employer code or private client data.

definitionOfDone: Codex can inspect and review a harmless change

stories.title: Create durable Codex instructions and project context
stories.outcome: Every Codex session begins with accurate working agreements and product context.
stories.context: Use the supplied global template and repository AGENTS.md. Create product, architecture, decisions, environment, debugging, and tools documents.
acceptanceCriteria: Global instructions cover safety and learning behavior without hard-coding one project's stack
Repository AGENTS.md defines Next.js commands, docs, quality gates, and secret rules
Codex reports the loaded instruction sources
Context documents have owners and update triggers
stories.dataContract: Markdown context documents; environment inventory contains names/owners only, never values.

expectations.security: No secret or personal path in committed instructions.
expectations.privacy: Project docs contain approved context only.
expectations.accessibility: Instructions require semantic and keyboard checks.

definitionOfDone: Codex follows and can summarize the instruction chain

stories.title: Give Codex GitHub and Vercel diagnostics
stories.outcome: Codex can inspect repository and deployment evidence from the local environment.
stories.context: Authenticate GitHub CLI and install/authenticate Vercel CLI. Use only harmless practice resources and start with read-only diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: gh auth status works without token output being committed
Vercel CLI can list deployments and inspect one practice deployment/build log
docs/TOOLS.md identifies safe read-only commands and mutating commands requiring explicit approval
The learner explains how CLI access gives Codex better evidence than a screenshot alone
stories.dataContract: Tool inventory and redacted diagnostic transcript.

expectations.security: No CLI token or env value in prompts/evidence.

nonGoals: Giving blanket approval for production mutation
definitionOfDone: Read-only diagnostics work from Codex's repository environment

stories.title: Evaluate documentation, browser, MCP, and future tools
stories.outcome: The learner can decide when an agent needs another tool and what trust it introduces.
stories.context: Compare a documentation website, Codex web search, browser/screenshot context, CLI, API, SDK, MCP server, and plugin. Do not install random MCP servers.
acceptanceCriteria: Each tool type is defined through a current-project example
Inventory lists data exposed, permissions, publisher, install/auth, read/write actions, and removal
At least one proposed tool is rejected as unnecessary
Supabase CLI and Playwright are deferred to the milestones that need them

expectations.security: Every new tool expands trust surface.
expectations.privacy: Identify data transmitted outside the machine.

nonGoals: Maximizing the number of installed tools

stories.title: Complete the teach-inspect-debug exercise
stories.outcome: Codex is used to learn and diagnose, not only generate code.
stories.context: Use a harmless failed Next.js practice deployment or fixture. Ask Codex to inspect project context and Vercel logs, teach the unfamiliar concept, cite primary docs, predict the fix, make a focused change, and review the diff.
acceptanceCriteria: Debugging packet contains expected, actual, reproduction, error, logs, attempts, and resolution
Codex cites primary docs relevant to the installed tool/framework version
The learner explains the cause back and answers a prediction question
An unnecessary generated change is rejected during diff review

expectations.accessibility: Resulting user failure state is understandable.

nonGoals: Copying a generated fix without explanation
